text: Agreed to pace rolling endurance rides steadily on climbs rather than surging, using conversational breathing and comfortable cadence to regulate the middle hours.
The final riser felt harder than usual; this was attributed to a headwind after a long day on the athlete's feet, not to declining fitness.
For exposed headwind sections, agreed to use a lower bar position and move snacks earlier to maintain final-hour energy, while monitoring hands and shoulders as volume increases.

Mild leg heaviness on day two of back-to-back rides cleared after 20 minutes of easy spinning; plan remains unchanged, but the second ride will be shortened if heaviness ever persists beyond 30 minutes.
For rides over two hours, agreed on one bottle per hour, food every 30 minutes, and a larger breakfast before sustained climbing; the routine will be practiced first on easy rides.
A recovery route with fewer junctions kept effort genuinely easy and breathing relaxed; recovery spins will therefore start from the park side of town and remain protected when the schedule is busy.
